rules: Exclude all duplicate policy IDs, not arbitrary first rows.

validation.holdout_design: One frozen policy-level random holdout, not out-of-time or prospective validation.
validation.concentration_definition: 1 - 2 integral(cumulative observed loss share against cumulative exposure share), ordered increasing selected premium prediction; exposure concentration index, not causal discrimination or normalized Gini.

uncertainty.method: Ordinary policy-cluster percentile bootstrap, pointwise 95%; fixed fitted models; no training or selection uncertainty.
uncertainty.warning: Heavy-tailed claims and one historical holdout can make bootstrap intervals unstable; no prospective or simultaneous coverage guarantee.

training_poisson_glm.method: NB2 alpha=max(sum((y-mu)^2-mu)/sum(mu^2),0), based on unpenalized Poisson training fitted count means; no test outcomes used.
training_poisson_glm.optimization_message: CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL

frequency_residuals.caution: Unconditional count variance also reflects exposure and risk heterogeneity. Zero mismatch alone does not establish zero inflation.

large_claim_sensitivity.method: Diagnostic Gamma alpha=.1 refit using training payment cap at training99percentile; validation-only assessment. Primary selection and all main scores remain uncapped.

severity_distribution.method: Training-only mean Pearson squared relative residual for Gamma shape; SD log relative payment for lognormal sigma. Both normalized to each cell mean in simulation.
severity_distribution.warning: Distributional assumptions do not establish reliable extreme-tail extrapolation.

reconciliation_sensitivity.primary_definition: Count-consistent known-payment cohort; missing payments excluded, not treated as zero.
reconciliation_sensitivity.warning: Different populations and claim definitions; this descriptive comparison does not estimate missing payment amounts or validate discarding them.

diagnostics.primary_data_scope: All EDA claims/costs/model metrics refer to strict reconciled economic cohort unless source audit is explicitly named.

explainability.warning: Conditional model associations and permutation effects, not causal effects or approved rating factors.

case_studies.title: Why exposure adjustment matters
case_studies.question: How do annual rates differ from claim probability?
case_studies.method: Annual rate is positive-payment count divided by exposure; fitted count = exposure × annual rate.
case_studies.result: Holdout observed rate 0.073654 payments per exposure-year; selected predicted rate 0.075156.
case_studies.limitation: Claim frequency permits multiple claims; it is not the proportion of policies with a claim.

case_studies.title: Poisson versus nonlinear and NB2 frequency
case_studies.question: Does a more flexible mean improve exposure-aware scores?
case_studies.method: All candidates use positive-payment annual-frequency target and exposure weights; validation deviance selects once.
case_studies.result: Selected Poisson HGB leaves=15; holdout Poisson deviance/exposure 0.449373. Training Pearson dispersion 1.781.
case_studies.limitation: Poisson scoring evaluates conditional means; this does not prove the full count distribution is Poisson.

case_studies.title: Gamma severity and large claims
case_studies.question: How sensitive is severity to the right tail?
case_studies.method: Individual positive payments inherit policy split; primary scores use every uncapped claim. A capped refit is a development-only diagnostic.
case_studies.result: Selected Gamma GLM alpha=0.1; holdout Gamma deviance 2.025686. Above-training-p99 payments contribute 35.2% of training paid cost.
case_studies.limitation: Good mean deviance does not validate Gamma extreme-tail behavior.

case_studies.title: Two-part pricing versus direct Tweedie
case_studies.question: Which approach scores better on the frozen common criterion?
case_studies.method: Compare all models with exposure-weighted Tweedie deviance at fixed p=1.5, including models trained with p=1.3/1.7.
case_studies.result: Selected Two-part frequency × severity; holdout common-p deviance 80.4632, observed/expected loss 1.1833.
case_studies.limitation: Direct Tweedie does not independently identify frequency and severity components; selected on validation only.

case_studies.title: Validation and policy-cluster uncertainty
case_studies.question: How uncertain are observed rates and calibration?
case_studies.method: Ordinary policy-cluster percentile bootstrap, pointwise 95%; fixed fitted models; no training or selection uncertainty.
case_studies.result: Holdout pure-premium percentile interval [125.10, 316.69] source units/exposure-year.
case_studies.limitation: Heavy-tailed claims and one historical holdout can make bootstrap intervals unstable; no prospective or simultaneous coverage guarantee.

case_studies.title: How portfolio composition changes mean cost
case_studies.question: How do synthetic profiles contribute different expected losses?
case_studies.method: Invented covariate profiles pass through the fixed training-fitted models; they are not identifiable source policies.
case_studies.result: Across eight illustrative one-year profiles, selected annual pure premium ranges 100.93–583.29 source units.
case_studies.limitation: Associations do not establish causal effects, allowed rating factors or real offers.

case_studies.title: Monte Carlo aggregate loss and tail assumptions
case_studies.question: How does the assumed severity tail change simulated portfolio risk?
case_studies.method: 10,000 aggregate simulations for 1,000 synthetic one-year policies; Gamma versus lognormal severity, matching fitted conditional means.
case_studies.result: Shared analytical expected loss 262,754.85 SMU. Gamma ES95 611,360.58; lognormal ES95 367,810.71. Mean-preserving shared frequency shock ES95 702,798.17.
case_studies.interpretation: Different distributional assumptions can materially change extreme-loss estimates even when expected losses agree.
case_studies.limitation: Hypothetical synthetic composition; fitted mean diagnostics do not establish a valid extreme tail. Monte Carlo and parameter uncertainties are different.

case_studies.title: Premium adequacy under hypothetical stress
case_studies.question: What happens when incidence and payment severity both rise while assumed premium stays fixed?
case_studies.method: Raise each component by20%; expected loss increases multiplicatively by1.44. Keep illustrative portfolio premium fixed.
case_studies.result: Baseline expected loss ratio 71.43%; frequency-only 85.71%; severity-only 85.71%; combined 102.86%.
case_studies.interpretation: An assumed premium cushion can be exhausted by compound stress; this is expected loss divided by hypothetical premium, not observed insurer profitability.
case_studies.limitation: No actual earned premiums, expenses, tax or profit observations. Stress sizes are assumptions rather than economic forecasts.

protocol.split: SHA256 seed:integerID; first64bits/2**64 <.6 train, <.8 validation, otherwise test
protocol.population: Unique policy identifiers, finite complete predictors, valid strictly positive exposure, nonnegative integer source claim count matching linked severity records, no missing or negative severity payments. No upper exposure or payment clipping.
protocol.frequency_target: Strictly positive payment count / exposure-year, exposure weighted; compatible with positive Gamma severity
protocol.severity_target: Individual strictly positive payment, all claims inherit policy split; zero-cost claims audited and excluded from BOTH positive-frequency count and severity target
protocol.preprocessing: Fixed log1p density, numeric training median and standard deviation, onehot(dropfirst) or ordinal training categories with explicit categorical HGB semantics; no target-derived transforms
protocol.frequency_candidates: Intercept; Poisson alpha0/.001/.1; Poisson HGB100iter lr.05 leaves7/15 minleaf100 L2=1, no early stopping; NB2 full training moment-dispersion diagnostic if Pearson>1.2
protocol.severity_candidates: Intercept; Gamma log GLM alpha0/.01/.1/1, individual unweighted claims
protocol.pure_premium_candidates: Selected frequency*selected severity; Tweedie log GLM p1.3/1.5/1.7 alpha.001/.1
protocol.selection: Minimum validation Poisson deviance per exposure for frequency; mean validation Gamma deviance for severity; minimum exposure-weighted Tweedie deviance at COMMON fixed power1.5 for premium (even for different fitted powers). Ties retain earlier simpler candidate. No refit after validation selection.
protocol.uncertainty: 250 ordinary policy-cluster bootstrap resamples, seed4242; pointwise percentile95%; fixed models, no tuning/training uncertainty, all claim costs/counts clustered in policies
protocol.sensitivity: Training-only payment99percentile cap diagnostic with validation capped and uncapped metrics; does not change primary full-cost population or selection. Training Gamma relative Pearson moment and lognormal logresidual SD for simulation shape assumptions.
protocol.test_policy: Evaluate only after all selection decisions; additional displayed diagnostics are descriptive, not used for reselection
protocol.currency: Source claim-amount monetary units; historical nominal values; no silent EUR conversion
protocol.limitations: Historical French MTPL; no reliable timestamps or prospective split, censoring/development unknown, strict reconciliation changes population, association not causality, no pricing/regulatory approval

limitations: Historical French MTPL sample; no reliable prospective or out-of-time validation; not current Nordic insurance experience.
Strict count-payment reconciliation excludes unresolved histories and can change selection/population composition.
Payment development, inflation, recoveries, deductibles, limits and missing payment histories are not fully known.
Large losses are retained; a small number dominate severity, calibration, uncertainty and simulated tails.
Pointwise bootstrap intervals condition on fitted models and ignore model-selection uncertainty.
Gamma/lognormal and Poisson risk assumptions are illustrative; model mean scores do not validate tail distributions.
Predictive demographic/geographic associations are not causal or evidence of pricing permissibility.
No insurer endorsement, underwriting approval, regulatory certification or production pricing claim.

reproducibility.cross_platform: Floating-point results may vary by BLAS/platform; exact bitwise cross-platform reproducibility not claimed.

simulation.portfolio_definition: Equal-weight mixture of eight synthetic one-year profiles; not a reconstruction of source records; uses selected two-part components even if direct Tweedie wins pricing selection.
assumptions: Synthetic equal-weight mixture of eight fitted profiles, 125 one-year policies of each type; composition scenario explicitly changes weights.
Poisson count means from selected frequency; Gamma/lognormal claim means from selected positive severity.
Gamma shape and lognormal log-residual scale estimated on training only; both severity alternatives normalized to the same conditional means.
Baseline conditional independence. Shared count-rate factor exp(sigma Z − sigma²/2) has mean one, preserves marginal expected loss and adds process variability; sigma0.35 is hypothetical.
All stresses and commercial premium loadings are hypothetical. SMU are source monetary units; no FX or inflation conversion.
Monte Carlo standard error is sample loss SD/sqrt(R). It describes numerical mean precision, not model parameter uncertainty or reliable tail-quantile precision.
VaR uses inverse empirical CDF; ES averages exact worst-tail probability mass with fractional boundary/tie handling. No Solvency II/regulatory capital claim.
simulation.tail_warning: Mean models do not validate severity tail distributions. Only 100 simulated portfolios lie in the 99% tail; estimates can be unstable and omit catastrophe, development, inflation and parameter uncertainty.
